clips.text: And college meant assignments. Lots of them. All typed by hand. No Wispr Flow back then. Just a keyboard, and very tired fingers.
Then I graduated. B.Com. Honours, Delhi University. Degree in hand. No idea what came next.
I didn’t know what job I wanted. But I knew I wanted to build something of my own.
I’d loved telling stories since childhood. Now I wanted to build products people would love using. So this commerce graduate decided to learn to code.
I’m still not sure where that confidence came from. No engineering degree. But I gave myself a chance to learn.
I spent the next year teaching myself how to build products. No job. From product decisions to code to getting it running. Whatever I didn’t understand, I learned.
Within a year, I could code reasonably well. A few internships followed. Everything was new, and every day brought something to learn.
Then I joined CaseBase as its second team member, in a founding product role. It was a generalist role. I wrote code, built features, and helped figure out what the product needed next.
That work took me to the US. I visited community service and community corrections organizations, meeting the people we were building for.
Today, I’m also working as a growth consultant for Anytime Fitness India. Different challenges. The same curiosity.
